source.authorityName: School examination paper (school not named); obtained from icseboard.org, originally from icseonline.com
source.notes: ICSE Class IX school final term examination paper (school not named). Header prints 'Final Term Examination 2017-2018', 'Std. : IX', 'Subject : Biology', 'Full Marks : 80', 'Time : 2Hrs.+15mins.'; examYear 2018 is the later year of the printed session (also the year in the file name). durationMinutes 135 = 2 h + 15 min as printed. The PDF has no text layer (watermark only); text was OCRed with RapidOCR and corrected against the page images. Section A (40 marks, compulsory) prints only group totals for groups I-VI, so each group is kept as one entry with that total (I is printed as 'I. (a) Name the following' with no (b)). Section B (40 marks, attempt any four) prints Q2-Q6; printed sub-part marks add up to 12 for Q2 and 10 for Q3-Q6. In Q3 the second sub-part is printed '(i)' again; it is labelled '(ii)' here. Q5 (i) is printed '[1+2]' and kept as one 3-mark entry. The seed diagram referred to in Q6 (i) is not printed in the PDF. The skin diagram in Q3 is not reproduced. No answer key is printed; no official answers exist.
source.usage: School examination paper published on icseboard.org (originally icseonline.com); question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to where it was obtained. Figures are not reproduced.

questions.text:
Name the following :
(i) The world organisation concerned with the supplying food and other facilities to children in schools.
(ii) The drug based on arsenic compound, produced in 1910 which killed germs of syphilis.
(iii) Inactivated toxin secreted by bacteria.
(iv) The body structure which protects the lungs from mechanical injuries.
(v) Maximum air which can at any time be held in the two lungs.
(vi) The skin glands which when inflamed cause acne.
(vii) The horny protein present in cornified layer of skin epidermis.
(viii) Part of plumule above the embryonic axis of the seed.
(ix) The layer of endosperm of maize, rich in protein.
(x) The resistance to the on set of a disease after infection by germs.
